figures.finding: An individual's salary and wage income is taxed at nothing on the first WST 15,000 a year, 20% from $15,001 to $25,000 and 27% above, the rates in force since 1 January 2018 and still published by the Ministry for Revenue.

sources.said: FORTNIGHTLY AND ANNUAL INCOME TAX RATES … The new fortnightly and annual tax deduction from salary & wage income applies to pay periods ending on and after 1 January 2018. FORTNIGHTLY TAX ANNUAL TAX $0 - $576 NIL $0 - $15,000 NIL $577 - $962 20% $15,001 - $25,000 20% Over $962 27% Over $25,000 27%

figures.finding: Employers deduct PAYE fortnightly: nothing to WST 576, 20% to $962 and 27% above.
figures.applies: Pay periods ending on or after 1 January 2018

sources.said: NOTICE TO EMPLOYERS … FORTNIGHTLY TAX ANNUAL TAX $0 - $576 NIL $0 - $15,000 NIL $577 - $962 20% $15,001 - $25,000 20% Over $962 27% Over $25,000 27%

figures.finding: The Ministry for Revenue's own 2025 return (filed in 2026) still taxes an individual's income at nothing to WST 15,000, 20% from 15,000 to 25,000 and WST 2,000 plus 27% above 25,000, the same schedule as 2018.
figures.applies: Individuals (sole traders and salary earners) for the 2025 income year, returns filed by 31 March 2026

sources.said: If the amount in box 21B is below $15,000 go straight to question 22 and enter $0.00 tax to pay in box 22A OR • If the amount in box 21B is over $15,000 and less than $25,000 use column 1 OR • If the amount in box 21B is over $25,000 please use column 2. … Subtract $15,000 from A and print answer in B … Multiply amount in B by 20% and print answer in C … Subtract $25,000 from A and print answer in B … Multiply amount in B by 27% and print answer in C … Add $2,000 to amount in C

figures.finding: The income year ends 31 December; the return and any tax are due by 31 March of the next year, and provisional tax for the following year is paid in three instalments on 31 March, 31 July and 31 October.
figures.applies: Individuals with a standard 31 December balance date

sources.said: Year Ended 31 Dec … Send your return to Inland Revenue Services, Box 1877, Apia on or before the 31st of March, unless you have an exten- sion of time or a non-standard balance date approved by the CEO of the Ministry for Revenue … If you have tax to pay, this is due by the 31st March 2026. … First provisional tax payment due 31 March 2026 … Second provisional tax payment due 31 July 2026 25B $ Third provisional tax payment due 31 October 2026

figures.finding: Every employer and every worker pays an Accident Compensation Corporation levy of 1 sene per tala of wages (1% each), with each pay run; the Samoa National Provident Fund contribution was not read.

sources.said: How much levy do I need to pay and when? Every employer and worker pays a levy of $0.01 sene for every $1.00 of wages. Payment time depends on how often wages are paid.

figures.finding: A business must register for VAGST once annual turnover passes WST 130,000, and files VAGST returns every two months; an unregistered person may not charge VAGST (the rate was not found on the Ministry's pages read).

sources.said: You are not permitted to charge VAGST on goods or services supplied if you are not registered for VAGST. … A taxable period is how often you file your VAGST returns which is two monthly. … [VAGST Threshold: $130,000 p.a]
